subject: LGM: Estimating effect on slope for specific variable at post measurement

messages.author: 7ddedfe56b1dad4a
messages.subject: LGM: Estimating effect on slope for specific variable at post measurement
parts:
Dear lavaan group, 

I´m using the lavaan package to estimate a latent growth model to analyse data of an intervention study with three measurement time points. The following model includes the covariates group (intervention vs. control group), gender and age.

model = '

  i =~ 1*t1_hrw + 1*t2_hrw + 1*t3_hrw
  s =~ 0*t1_hrw + 7*t2_hrw + 9*t3_hrw
  t1_hrw ~~ a*t1_hrw                   
  t2_hrw ~~ a*t2_hrw                     
  t3_hrw ~~ a*t3_hrw                    
  i ~ group + gender + age
  s ~ group + gender + age
'

Additionally I want to examine the effect on the slope specifically for my group covariate (intervention vs. control group) at post-measurement t2. To what extent would the code be specified to achieve this intent?

Any help is well appreciated! Thank you very much in advance
Sophie

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: LGM: Estimating effect on slope for specific variable at post measurement
parts: a latent growth model to analyse data of an intervention study with three measurement time points

From your description below ("post-measurement"), this sounds like a pretest, posttest, follow-up design.  A linear growth model is probably not appropriate for that.  You generally expect a pre-post change, then either no change at follow-up or (often) diminished effect (so closer to pretest level, i.e., "growth" in the opposite direction).

Perhaps a latent difference score (LDS) model is more appropriate, in which case you can regress the latent difference scores (changes) on covariates.  
Or investigate "residualized change" by regressing both posttests on the pretest (as well as covariates) and looking for (adjusted) mean differences to test whether posttest levels are consistent.

Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
